Only two symbols have to change. The decorator needs no code change.

**Required**

1. `src/click/core.py:Option.__init__` (line 2897). It has an explicit keyword list and passes everything else through `**attrs` to `Parameter.__init__`. An unknown `sensitive=` would therefore reach `Parameter.__init__` and raise `TypeError`. It needs a new `sensitive: bool = False` parameter and `self.sensitive = sensitive`, next to `self.hide_input`. Also add the class-level annotation (`sensitive: bool`, near line 2882) and a `:param sensitive:` docstring entry.

2. `src/click/core.py:Option.to_info_dict` (line 3062). Add `sensitive=self.sensitive` to the `info_dict.update(...)` call so the flag is visible. The redaction also has to happen here, because the value lives in the `"default"` key (and possibly `"flag_value"`). `Parameter.to_info_dict` (line 2325) builds `"default"` and `Option.to_info_dict` calls `super()` first. So after the `super()` call, `Option.to_info_dict` should overwrite `info_dict["default"]` and `flag_value` with a placeholder or `None` when `self.sensitive` is true.

**Optional**

- `src/click/core.py:Parameter.to_info_dict` (line 2325). Only touch it if you want redaction there instead. It builds `"default"` and has no access to `sensitive`, because that attribute would live on `Option`. Doing the redaction in `Option` is simpler and doesn't affect `Argument`.

**Not needed**

- `src/click/decorators.py:option` (line 352). It does `cls(param_decls, **attrs)`, so `sensitive=True` reaches `Option.__init__` unchanged. At most, update the docstring.
- `Parameter.__init__`. `sensitive` is consumed by `Option.__init__` before `**attrs` is forwarded.
- `Command.to_info_dict` (line 1076), `Group.to_info_dict` (line 1715) and `Context.to_info_dict` (line 524). They only call `param.to_info_dict()` on each parameter.
- `Argument.to_info_dict` (line 3593). It only applies if you also want arguments to be sensitive.
- `types.py`. The `type` sub-dict holds no values.
